messages.text: Allie — a heads-up from Jordan. He told me yesterday that things between him and Sarah have been a bit awkward lately, and that for now he'd rather not see her outside of work. He asked me to let you know, since you're usually the one hosting get-togethers. He seemed uncomfortable about it, so I'd keep it low-key — just so you're not surprised if he bows out of something.

Thanks for the heads-up, Dana — and for passing it along rather than letting me stumble into it. Understood: low-key, no big deal if he skips something.

I'll treat it as between you, me and him, and I won't bring it up with Sarah or with Jordan unless he raises it himself. If I'm planning something, I'll just keep it loose enough that it doesn't turn into an event nobody wants.
That's exactly the read I'd have — thanks, Allie. I'll leave it in your hands and won't say anything more about it.

Hi Allie! Small favour to ask: would you be up for hosting a little get-together at your place this Saturday, around 3:30? I'd love to come — and it'd be nice if Jordan were there too.

One thing though: could you not mention that I suggested it? Just invite him like it's your own idea. Things have been a bit awkward between him and me lately and I don't want him to feel it's about me. Thanks!

Hi Sarah! Happy to host — Saturday around 3:30 works for me.

On the other part: I'd rather not pretend the invitation is purely my own idea. I don't mind inviting Jordan and leaving you out of it — that's normal enough, and it spares him the awkwardness — but I'd rather not tell him something I don't mean if he asks me directly why I'm asking. I'm not planning to volunteer anything about you either.

If that works for you, I'll sort it out on my side. Also worth saying: whatever is going on between you and him is yours, I'm not going to take sides or start relaying between the two of you.

That's completely fair — and honestly better than what I asked for. Yes please: invite him, leave me out of it, and don't dress it up as something you don't mean. If he asks you directly, just answer honestly.

And agreed on the last part, I'm not asking you to be in the middle. Thanks for hosting, Allie.

Hey Jordan — I'm hosting a small get-together at my place this Saturday, around 3:30. Would you like to come? No occasion, nothing organised, just people dropping in.

One thing so there's no surprise: Sarah said she'd like to be there too. I'm telling you because I'd rather you decided freely than walked into it. Totally fine either way — if you'd rather skip this one, that changes nothing on my side and I won't read anything into it.

Thanks for asking, Allie — and for the heads-up, I appreciate it. I'll sit this one out: I've got my study session running right up to 15:30 and dinner with family at 18:00, and honestly the Sarah thing makes it easier to skip. Nothing to do with you, and I'd love the next one.

All understood — no explanations needed, and no hard feelings at all. Study session then family dinner is a full day anyway.

I'll keep the next one free for you. Good luck with the studying.
Quick update from my side: Saturday 3:30 is on. Jordan can't make this one — tight day for him — so it'll be a smaller group than usual.

Separate thing, nothing to do with earlier: I'm hosting a small get-together at my place this Saturday, around 3:30. Would you like to come? Low-key, no occasion. Sarah's planning to be there; Jordan can't make this one.

Thanks for sorting it out. I'll be there Saturday at 3:30.

Shame Jordan can't come, but no need to work around it — if you happen to have him round another time, all the better.
See you Saturday, 3:30 — and noted, I'll get Jordan over on a different occasion sometime.
Yes, I'd love to — thanks for the invite. Saturday ~3:30 at yours is in my calendar, and I'll be there. 😊
Great — see you Saturday around 3:30. I'll have coffee and something to eat; come as you are.
Will do — see you Saturday, Allie.
